commits.messageBody:
An independent clean-context review re-derived every load-bearing claim this
wi wrote down and disproved two of them. Both were comments, both carried a
"measured" label they had not earned, and a "measured" label is an exemption
coupon: the next reader has no reason to doubt it. Comment-only change; the
parsed CI workflow is byte-identical and the diff contains zero non-comment
lines.

web/tsconfig.app.json header: the claim that adding `composite: true` would
silently stop the build from emitting does not reproduce in this project. Both
referenced projects set `noEmit: true`, so no `tsc -b` invocation here is an
emitter at all (a bare `tsc -b` exits 0 producing zero .js/.d.ts and no dist/);
dist/ comes from `vite build`, whose emit does not depend on buildinfo state.
Adding composite three ways and running CI's own step bodies leaves dist/ at its
normal 6 files every time. The prohibition is kept, with its honest reason: the
premise doing the work is "no tsc here emits", nothing enforces that premise,
and the poisoning adjacency is already wired in ci.yml — so banning composite
keeps a future change that makes tsc an emitter from having to re-derive this.
That last hop is labelled as not re-measured, because it cannot be measured
while the premise still holds.

.github/workflows/ci.yml, `Typecheck web`: "the step below is the one that can
go red on a weakened typecheck" is false. The coverage step runs `tsc -b
--listFiles` itself and never invokes the script, so a `"typecheck": "true"`
body is structurally invisible to it — measured, that body leaves this step,
the coverage step and Build web all green, i.e. nothing goes red. The honest
scope is that the script's existence is load-bearing (deleting the key exits
254) and that type errors are gated by Build web, which predates this PR. The
step-order comment's "a `tsc -b` that must emit" is corrected the same way.
commits.messageHeadline: Downgrade two claims these gates could not support (tether#174)
